title: Hypertension
subtitle: High blood pressure, often called the silent killer because it has no obvious symptoms but significantly increases the risk of heart attack, stroke, and kidney failure.

sections.title: Symptoms
sections.intro: Hypertension is one of the most common chronic conditions worldwide, affecting 1 in 3 adults. Most people do not know they have it because it typically causes no symptoms until serious damage has occurred.
items: Usually no symptoms, known as the silent killer
Severe headaches (hypertensive crisis)
Dizziness and nosebleeds in very high BP
Shortness of breath and chest pain
Visual changes and blurred vision
Blood in urine (sign of kidney damage)

sections.title: Causes
sections.intro: Blood pressure is consistently above 130/80 mmHg. Primary hypertension develops gradually over years; secondary hypertension has a specific underlying cause.
items: Primary hypertension, genetic factors, age, lifestyle, obesity
Secondary, kidney disease, thyroid disorders, sleep apnea
High salt diet, physical inactivity, excessive alcohol
Chronic stress, smoking, and certain medications

sections.title: Prevention
items: Reduce salt intake to less than 5g per day
Follow DASH diet, rich in fruits, vegetables, whole grains
Exercise 30 minutes daily, brisk walking lowers BP
Maintain healthy weight, BMI 18.5, 24.9
Limit alcohol to 1-2 units per day maximum
Stop smoking and manage stress through relaxation techniques

sections.title: Treatment
items: ACE inhibitors (e.g. Lisinopril), relax blood vessels
ARBs (e.g. Losartan), block angiotensin, lower BP
Calcium channel blockers (e.g. Amlodipine), widen arteries
Diuretics (water pills), reduce fluid volume
Beta-blockers for specific cases
Regular monitoring with home blood pressure device
